blocks.cap: The Axis comes up between them without being called, and reaches for both brothers at the seam

blocks.p: The Axis surfaced the way weather surfaces. Rei did not summon it. It arrived.

It came up through the one register the two brothers shared, the Uedera grain under both their suppressions, the shape the far shore had found in Rei's hand when it sent him into the tear and keyed the two of them to a single office. Rei had first felt it as a balance, a fulcrum, a single living point that two suppressed registers leaned on from either side. On the thin night he understood it differently. It was the only thing in the city that did not want either of them in the chair.

It came up between them and the wound and it reached, in two directions at once. For the register that was Rei's. For the register that was left of Gin's. Against every line of the Healer's arithmetic, it tried to hold both of them off the seat by holding both of them up.

For one impossible second it worked. The chair asked and neither register answered, because the Axis had them both, balanced and suspended. Two brothers held an inch above the chair by the thing in them that refused to let the other fall.
In that second Rei saw it.

Not a force. A face. It was there and gone at the centre of the light, the way a face is there in a window at night when the room behind the glass is lit. A young man, thirty perhaps, in a dark plain coat of a cut nobody had worn for a hundred and fifty years. His hair was tied back. His expression was serene and attentive and very tired. He was looking at Rei the way a man looks at a word he once knew and loved and has lost the meaning of. He had his back to everything else. His whole attention was on the wall.

Gin's book had said it in its clinical way, in the pages he could not prove. It answers one question per approach. It does not show its face. It returns the practitioner. It was showing its face. It was not returning anyone. It was too busy holding two people up.

Rei had one question. He knew the rule. He did not ask how to save Gin, or which of them the chair would take, or how long the wall would hold. He asked the thing he had wanted to ask since the shove.
"What are you holding?"
The answer did not come in words. It came as the shape of an old word sitting down inside him. The seat I became.

Rei stored it next to the half-sentence Gin had spent his last lucid strength on in the kitchen. The chair doesn't need a new occupant. It needs its old one. He did not understand it yet. He knew he would.
Then the Axis began to stretch.

Rei felt what Higuchi's smallest letters had never had room to say. The Axis was built to bear one. It was a fulcrum, not a bridge. It held the city's balance the way a knife-edge holds a scale, and a knife-edge asked to carry both pans at once does not balance. It bows. Rei felt it bow inside his chest. The shared register went taut and thin and bright like the seam over the river. The two of them were held, but they were held by a thing that was paying for the holding in the only coin it had, which was itself.

It had been paying already, Rei understood. Since 2009 it had carried the thirteenth seat directly from the centre, with no living holder to take the weight. An Axis that overstretched made errors. The thinning Kita had suffered for six years was partly the sound of a man at the centre holding too much, too long.

The Healer watched this with an attention that was, for the first time all month, genuinely surprised. It had not planned for the Axis to refuse the chair. It had planned for the shared register to be the very thing that made one of them fit the chair. Now that register was straining itself to splinters to keep both of them out of the seat the Healer had spent so long preparing. For the first time, Rei had made the trap do something it did not intend.
The cost of that was that he could feel, exactly, how long the Axis could keep it up. Not long.

"Ah," the Healer said, soft, in his brother's tired voice. The surprise in it curdled slowly into something like respect. "You would do that. Of course you would. You would rather burn the fulcrum than let it choose. You would rather both of you fall than either of you sit, because to you the unbearable thing was never the open chair. It was being made to pick. I did account for your love, Rei. I built the whole engine on it. I did not account for your love taking this shape. The shape that would rather end the thing that connects you than let it hand down a verdict."
Across the water Kaito tilted his borrowed head, interested, the way a cat is interested in a bird that has flown into a window.

The seam over the river answered the strain. It thinned faster. The two cities slid another degree out of register, because the Axis was spending itself, and the wall read the spending the way the holders read everything, as a seam under load.

"But understand what you are doing," the Healer said. "The Axis is what has kept the wound honest. Stretch it to breaking and the chair does not close. It tears. There is no seat left to fill, only a hole, and a city does not survive an unmade office any better than a vacant one. You have found the one move I did not see. It is also the one move that ends with no door at all."
